Bayesian predictor-subset selection with brms and LOO

Source: R/fs_bayes.R
fs_bayes.Rd

Fits one brms model for each candidate combination of predictors, estimates each model's out-of-sample fit with PSIS-LOO, and picks a combination from the loo::loo_compare() table. The selected brmsfit is returned as the model of an fs_result.

Usage

fs_bayes(
  data,
  target,
  predictors,
  date_col = NULL,
  brm_family = stats::gaussian(),
  prior = NULL,
  brm_args = list(),
  rule = c("1se", "best"),
  max_comb_size = NULL,
  sample_combinations = NULL,
  parallel_combinations = FALSE,
  seed = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  n_cores = 1L
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame or data.table. It is copied, never modified. Only target, predictors, and date_col are kept, and rows with a missing value in any of them are dropped before any model is fitted. Infinite values in those columns are an error. None of those columns may be named fitted_values, residuals, abs_residuals, or squared_residuals, because those columns are appended to details$data.

target

Name of the target (response) column. It must exist in data and suit brm_family: numeric for stats::gaussian(), 0/1 or logical for brms::bernoulli().

predictors

Character vector naming the candidate predictor columns: at least one, without duplicates, all present in data.

date_col

Name of a date column, or NULL. When given, an iso_week_id feature (ISO year * 100 + ISO week) is added to the predictors, so no target, predictor, or date column may itself be named iso_week_id. iso_week_id enters the models as a continuous covariate, a rough encoding of seasonality; a categorical or cyclic encoding may come in a future version. The date column itself is never used as a predictor. Default NULL (no date feature).

brm_family

A model family accepted by brms::brm(), for example stats::gaussian() (the default) or brms::bernoulli().

prior

A brms prior specification. Default NULL (the brms default priors).

brm_args

List of extra arguments for brms::brm(), such as iter, warmup, or seed. They override featR's defaults of iter = 2000, adapt_delta = 0.99, max_treedepth = 15, and refresh = 0. chains and cores are respected when combinations are evaluated sequentially (the defaults are 4 chains on 1 core, and cores is capped at the detected core count), but both are forced to 1 when parallel_combinations = TRUE. The PSIS-LOO step uses the same core count, never getOption("mc.cores"). Default list().

rule

Selection rule. "1se" (default) keeps the most parsimonious model within one standard error of the best elpd; "best" keeps the raw elpd maximum. See Details.

max_comb_size

Largest number of predictors in a combination, a whole number >= 1, or NULL. Values above the number of candidate predictors are capped. Default NULL (all sizes).

sample_combinations

Number of combinations to draw at random instead of evaluating all of them, a whole number >= 1, or NULL. Ignored when fewer combinations exist. Pass seed to make the draw reproducible. Default NULL (evaluate every combination).

parallel_combinations

Logical. If TRUE, evaluate combinations in parallel with parallel::mclapply(). Each model is then limited to a single MCMC chain, so cross-chain convergence diagnostics such as R-hat are unavailable; a warning says so. On Windows, or when n_cores resolves to 1, evaluation falls back to sequential with a message. Default FALSE.

seed

Optional whole number within the R integer range; fractional values are an error. When supplied, the whole call runs on a local RNG stream and your RNG state is restored on exit. The seed drives the random draw of combinations (see sample_combinations) and, unless brm_args$seed is given, one Stan seed per combination, so the MCMC fits are reproducible too, including with parallel_combinations = TRUE. An explicit brm_args$seed is used for every model instead. Default NULL: fs_bayes() never seeds the RNG unless you ask, and brms and rstan then draw their seeds from the global stream.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE, print progress and every per-model warning, and show a progress bar for sequential evaluation when the suggested package 'pbapply' is installed. Default FALSE.

n_cores

Number of workers when parallel_combinations = TRUE, a whole number >= 1; ignored otherwise. Requests are capped at the detected core count. Default 1 (sequential).

Value

An object of class fs_result with:

selected

Character vector of the predictors in the chosen model.

scores

NULL, because no per-feature score is comparable across models with different predictors. details$n_features records how many candidate predictors were offered.

method

"bayes".

task

"classification" when brm_family is a binary, categorical, or ordinal family (bernoulli, binomial, beta_binomial, categorical, multinomial, cumulative, sratio, cratio, acat), otherwise "regression".

model

The selected brmsfit.

details

A list with:

  • data: the complete-case modeling data.table (target, predictors, and date_col and iso_week_id where applicable), with fitted_values, residuals, abs_residuals, and squared_residuals columns appended. Families without a single fitted value per row (categorical, multinomial, and multivariate responses) get no appended columns.

  • mae, rmse: in-sample errors on the rows used to fit and select, so optimistic; NA for the families without a single fitted value per row.

  • formula: the selected model's formula, as a string.

  • best_elpd: the selected model's elpd_loo, possibly NA; optimistic because it was selected (see Details).

  • loo_comparison: the loo::loo_compare() table (a matrix or a data.frame, depending on the loo version), or NULL when fewer than two models could be compared or the comparison failed.

  • n_failed_fits: how many combinations failed to fit.

  • n_loo_failed: how many fitted models were left out because loo() failed.

  • n_compared: how many models with a finite elpd_loo competed in the selection.

  • n_features: the number of candidate predictors, including iso_week_id when date_col is given.

call

The matched call.

Details

PSIS-LOO (Pareto-smoothed importance sampling leave-one-out) approximates leave-one-out cross-validation from a single posterior fit. It yields elpd_loo, an estimate of the expected log predictive density for new data; higher is better. Use fs_bayes() when you want the predictor subset chosen by that criterion under a fully Bayesian model and can afford one model per subset.

Cost of the search

The search is exhaustive by default. With p candidate predictors it fits every non-empty subset, 2^p - 1 models, and each one compiles and samples its own Stan program: 4 predictors mean 15 models, 10 predictors mean 1023. Use max_comb_size or sample_combinations to bound the search, and parallel_combinations to spread it over cores.

How a model is chosen

With rule = "1se" (the default), the chosen model is the one with the fewest predictors, ties broken by the higher elpd, among those whose elpd difference from the best model is at most one standard error of that difference (the se_diff column of the comparison table) in absolute value. With rule = "best", the raw elpd maximum wins; that was the older behavior and is more prone to over-fitting the comparison. When no usable comparison table is available, both rules fall back to the raw elpd maximum, ties broken by fewer predictors.

Failures and diagnostics

Combinations whose model fails to fit are left out of the selection, counted in details$n_failed_fits, and reported in a warning that quotes the first brms error. Fitted models for which loo::loo() fails or gives no finite elpd are left out in the same way, counted in details$n_loo_failed, and reported in a warning. If loo::loo_compare() itself fails, a warning says that the raw elpd maximum is used and rule = "1se" is not applied. If no fit yields a finite elpd_loo at all, the first successfully fitted model is returned with a warning. That model is an arbitrary fallback that no criterion chose.

Sampler warnings (divergent transitions, R-hat, effective sample size) and loo's Pareto-k warnings are muffled while the models are fitted, so a search over many subsets does not flood the console. They are counted instead: after the search, one warning reports how many fits raised sampler warnings and another how many have observations with Pareto k > 0.7 (unreliable PSIS-LOO estimates), and each says whether the selected model is among them. verbose = TRUE shows every individual warning.

What is optimistic

details$mae and details$rmse are in-sample errors, computed on the same rows used to fit and to select, so they are optimistic.

details$best_elpd and the loo_comparison table are optimistic too. PSIS-LOO is roughly unbiased for one fixed model, but the selected model's elpd_loo is the maximum (or, under rule = "1se", a near-maximum) over details$n_compared candidates. It therefore overstates the chosen model's out-of-sample performance, and more so the larger the search (selection-induced bias; Piironen and Vehtari, 2017). An honest estimate needs the whole search repeated inside an outer cross-validation, or held-out data.

Anything read off the returned brmsfit, such as posterior intervals or effect sizes, is post-selection inference: the model was chosen using the same data it is reported on. The Validation and leakage article covers both points.

References

Piironen, J. and Vehtari, A. (2017). Comparison of Bayesian predictive methods for model selection. Statistics and Computing, 27(3), 711-735.

See also

The Wrapper methods guide, which runs this function on a worked example.

Examples

# Fitting needs more than the brms package: brms compiles and samples a
# Stan program for each candidate model, which requires a working C++
# toolchain. The call is therefore guarded on brms being installed, limited
# to two single-predictor fits via max_comb_size = 1, and wrapped in try()
# so that a machine without a usable Stan toolchain skips the example
# instead of failing it.
# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("brms", quietly = TRUE)) {
  x1 <- seq(-2, 2, length.out = 40)
  x2 <- rep(c(-1, 1), 20)
  d <- data.frame(
    y  = 1 + 2 * x1 + sin(seq_len(40)),
    x1 = x1,
    x2 = x2
  )
  res <- try(
    fs_bayes(
      d, target = "y", predictors = c("x1", "x2"),
      max_comb_size = 1,
      brm_args = list(chains = 1, iter = 500, refresh = 0),
      rule = "1se", verbose = FALSE
    ),
    silent = TRUE
  )
  if (!inherits(res, "try-error")) {
    print(res$selected)
    print(res$details$loo_comparison)
  }
}
#> Compiling Stan program...
#> Compiling Stan program...
#> Warning: 2 of 2 model fits failed and were excluded from selection. First error (y ~ x1): Boost not found; call install.packages('BH')
# }
